propositions.text: The claimant is a Gabonese citizen claiming refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: The claimant, XXXX XXXX, a citizen of Gabon, is basing his claim for refugee protection on section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant, a Gabonese citizen, bases his refugee claim on IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).

propositions.text: The claimant was hired in 1995 in Gabon where mining is main industry; problems began in 2007 after founding protest group.
propositions.quote: The claimant was hired in 1995 in the city of XXXX, Gabon, where the main industry is mining. His problems began around 2007, following the founding of a group of protesters whose goal was to denounce the violation of ecological rules and the cancellation of workers' medical coverage at the company's hospital.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant was hired in 1995 in Gabon's mining city; problems began in 2007 after founding a protest group, says claimant.

propositions.text: In 2008, claimant raised awareness in villages; during protest he was arrested and beaten by soldiers and police.
propositions.quote: In 2008, he XXXX XXXX to raise awareness in the neighbouring villages. During a protest on XXXX, 2008, soldiers arrested him and took him to the police station, where he was beaten with police batons.

propositions.text: Hours later, claimant was forced into military vehicle and taken to military base.
propositions.quote: Only a few hours later, he was forced into a military vehicle and taken to the military base in XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant says in 2008 he raised awareness, was arrested, beaten, and taken to military base during protest.

propositions.text: A high-ranking officer asked claimant's ethnicity; upon learning they shared ethnicity, officer helped release him.
propositions.quote: During the trip, one of the high-ranking officers who was watching him asked him what ethnic group he belonged to. When the claimant told him that he was of the XXXX ethnic group, this man promised to release him, since he was of the same ethnicity.

propositions.text: Claimant was released with officer's help and hitchhiked home; asked wife to get Canadian visitor invitation letter.
propositions.quote: Thus, the claimant was released with this man's help and hitchhiked home. When he arrived, he asked his wife to contact a friend in Canada and have him send a letter of invitation as a visitor to Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant says officer of same ethnicity helped release him; he hitchhiked home and asked wife to get Canadian invitation letter.

propositions.text: In 2008, claimant went to Cameroon to apply for Canadian visa, got it in 8 days, returned secretly to Gabon, then travelled to Canada.
propositions.quote: On XXXX, 2008, he went to Cameroon to file his application at the Canadian High Commission. He received his visa eight days later. He returned to Gabon in secret. On XXXX, 2008, he travelled to XXXX, and then arrived in Montréal on XXXX, 2008.

propositions.text: Claimant claimed Canada's protection on XXXX, 2008.
propositions.quote: He claimed Canada's protection on XXXX, 2008.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant applied for Canadian visa in Cameroon, returned secretly to Gabon, then arrived in Canada and claimed protection.

propositions.text: The panel finds claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection for reasons that follow.
propositions.quote: Having heard the claimant's testimony and analyzed all of the evidence on file, the panel determines that the claimant is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection," for the reasons that follow.

paragraphs.summary: The panel determines claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: Claimant says he founded protest group to get free medical care and denounce ecological violations.
propositions.quote: To begin, the claimant states in his narrative that he founded a group of protesters for the purpose of reaching the majority of people living in the villages in order to obtain free medical care and benefits, and also to denounce the violation of ecological rules.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant states he founded protest group to obtain free medical care and denounce ecological violations.

propositions.text: Claimant said group had no name and no letter copy; panel finds claims insufficient and doubts membership.
propositions.quote: In light of these responses, the panel is of the opinion that his claims about XXXX XXXX are wholly insufficient, and the panel strongly doubts that he was a member of this pressure group.

paragraphs.summary: Panel doubts claimant's protest group membership due to lack of name and letter copy.

propositions.text: Claimant said three other protesters disappeared, two returned to work; panel notes this.
propositions.quote: He testified that, according to the union, three of these people were considered disappeared, as they had not responded to the call that was sent out to them. He stated that the other two people had been able to go back to work for the company.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified three other protesters disappeared, two returned to work, noted by panel.

propositions.text: Panel asked why two protesters returned to work but claimant got death threats; claimant said due to ethnicity and role.
propositions.quote: The panel asked him why the other two people, who had been responsible, as XXXX, for the protest on XXXX, 2008, had been able to return to work, whereas he had received death threats. The claimant responded that he thought he had been threatened because he was a XXXX in the XXXX XXXX mining company.

propositions.text: A document shows local union led protests against mining company pollution and medical coverage cancellation.
propositions.quote: A document dated XXXX, 2008,1 (an article entitled "Gabon : Moanda pointe du doigt la pollution de la COMILOG" [Gabon: Moanda denounces COMILOG pollution]) clearly states the following: [Translation] [L]ed by the local representative of the Union gabonaise pour la démocratie et le développement [Gabonese Union for Democracy and Development], inhabitants of the mining city of Moanda in the province of Haut-Ogooué protested vehemently against the Comilog mining company's violation of ecological rules, at a recent meeting of the company's governing board.

paragraphs.summary: Panel questioned why two protesters returned to work but claimant got threats; document shows local union led protests.

propositions.text: Claimant said local union rep was from different province; panel rejects this and finds claimant unaware of known protest.
propositions.quote: The claimant responded that the representative was not from the same province as him, that he was from XXXX, XXXX. The panel does not accept the claimant's testimony, as this representative was inciting the inhabitants of XXXX to protest against XXXX. It is clear that the claimant was not aware of this well-known protest led by the local representative.

paragraphs.summary: Panel rejects claimant's claim about union rep's province and finds claimant unaware of known protest.

propositions.text: Claimant said he never contacted employer and lost job due to company's negative view of him.
propositions.quote: In addition, when he was asked whether he had left or quit his job, the claimant stated that he had never contacted his employer at work and that, according to the information he had received from the union, he had lost his job because the company took a negative view of him.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant said he lost job due to company's negative view and never contacted employer.

propositions.text: Claimant went twice to Cameroon for Canadian visa, returned to Cameroon without settling; panel doubts fear of return to Gabon.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, after obtaining a letter of invitation from a Canadian he had allegedly met in XXXX while he was working at the mine, the claimant went to XXXX to obtain his Canadian visa. He therefore went to XXXX twice to obtain his Canadian visa, and returned to XXXX without even trying to settle in XXXX.

propositions.text: Claimant said he did not claim asylum in Cameroon because he would not be safe; panel finds voluntary return inconsistent with fear.
propositions.quote: When the panel asked him why he had not considered staying in XXXX, he answered that he had not intended to claim asylum there, and then added that he would not have been safe in XXXX and that that was why he had returned to XXXX, a country where he claims he was being persecuted.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant went twice to Cameroon for visa, returned without settling; panel doubts fear of return to Gabon.

propositions.text: Claimant's explanation for not claiming asylum on arrival in Canada was unsatisfactory.
propositions.quote: In addition, the claimant's response regarding why he had not claimed refugee protection upon his arrival in Canada on XXXX, 2008, was not satisfactory in the panel's opinion.

propositions.text: Claimant said he planned to stay and work and did not realize procedures to follow.
propositions.quote: The claimant had previously testified that he would be a dead man if he returned to his country. When asked to explain his conduct, he stated that he had planned to stay here and work and that he had not realized that there were procedures to follow.

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds claimant's explanation for not claiming asylum on arrival unsatisfactory.

propositions.text: Panel does not believe claimant fears return; voluntary return twice undermines fear claim.
propositions.quote: Once again, the panel does not believe that the claimant has a fear of returning. His entire testimony leads the panel to believe that he came here to have access to better economic opportunities because, as noted above, if he feared for his life, he would have claimed protection immediately, the moment he arrived in Canada.

propositions.text: Case law holds voluntary return to country inconsistent with well-founded fear of persecution.
propositions.quote: Moreover, the panel notes in this regard that the case law has consistently held that a refugee protection claimant's voluntary return to their country of nationality is inconsistent with a well-founded fear of persecution.

paragraphs.summary: Panel disbelieves claimant's fear of return; case law says voluntary return inconsistent with fear of persecution.

propositions.text: Claimant failed to discharge burden of proof; refugee claim is rejected.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant has not discharged his burden of proof. Consequently, the claim for refugee protection filed by XXXX XXXX is rejected.

paragraphs.summary: Panel concludes claimant failed burden of proof and rejects refugee claim.
